cfpb_hmda_modified_lar_2017_to_2018.rationale: The source codes identify the federal supervisory/regulatory agency (OCC, FRS, FDIC, NCUA, HUD, CFPB). No selected 2018 target field identifies that agency; the LEI identifies a legal entity, and loan type/purpose identify the loan.
cfpb_hmda_modified_lar_2017_to_2018.absence_scope: All selected target dictionary fields; complete official 2018 Modified LAR dictionary also has no Agency Code field.

negative_contrasts.official_basis: 2018 dictionary field heading Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)
2018 codes classify insurance/guarantee status, not supervisory agency.

cfpb_hmda_modified_lar_2017_to_2018.rationale: Both official codesheets define the same insurance/guarantee loan type, with the conventional/FHA/VA/FSA-RHS categories preserved.

Both dictionaries designate Loan Amount. The 2017 filing specification says report in thousands; the 2018 dictionary publishes dollar midpoint values for $10000 intervals. Match the measure, with unit conversion and changed disclosure precision explicitly recorded.
The 2017 Preapprovals codesheet and 2018 Preapproval codesheet both distinguish whether preapproval was requested. The 2018 code domain removes the older not-applicable code.
The eight official action categories align, including originated, approved but not accepted, denied, withdrawn, incomplete, purchased, and preapproval disposition.

The 2017 specification explicitly identifies an MSA or metropolitan-division code. The 2018 dictionary has state, county and census-tract identifiers, and no MSA/MD field. Those are distinct geographic levels.
cfpb_hmda_modified_lar_2017_to_2018.absence_scope: All selected target fields; complete official 2018 Modified LAR dictionary also has no MSA/MD field.

cfpb_hmda_modified_lar_2017_to_2018.rationale: The source applicant ethnicity field and target first applicant/borrower ethnicity slot have the same person role and core ethnicity categories. The first target slot preserves information-not-provided and not-applicable codes.
The source co-applicant ethnicity field and target first co-applicant/co-borrower ethnicity slot retain the same person role, including the no-co-applicant category.
Both published names identify the first race slot for the applicant. The target first slot retains the source missing/not-applicable categories while adding detailed race categories.
Both published names identify the first race slot for the co-applicant. The target first slot retains missing/not-applicable/no-co-applicant categories while adding detailed race categories.
Both codesheets define sex for the applicant, with male/female/information-not-provided/not-applicable categories. The target separately adds a both-selected category.
Both codesheets define sex for the co-applicant, retaining the no-co-applicant role distinction. The target separately adds a both-selected category.
Both official codesheets classify the purchaser of a loan. The institution categories are preserved conceptually, with the older combined code-7 category split into codes 71 and 72.

Both dictionaries identify the first denial-reason slot. Codesheets independently list the same core debt-to-income, employment, credit, collateral, cash, unverifiable, incomplete, insurance and other categories.

The same published Rate Spread field appears in both versions. The 2017 specification independently provides a decimal-string example; the 2018 dictionary declares a character-varying field with NA and Exempt sentinels.
Both versions explicitly name HOEPA Status. The 2017 codes distinguish HOEPA loan versus not; the 2018 codes distinguish high-cost mortgage versus not and add not-applicable.
Both codesheets explicitly classify first versus subordinate liens. The target removes two older extra statuses, so matching the concept does not promise a lossless recode.

adyen_classic_payment52_to_checkout72.rationale: Both independently define the delay between payment authorization and automatic capture, explicitly in hours.
Both independently state the shopper date of birth and YYYY-MM-DD. Their declared schema formats differ; the semantic field matches while the inconsistent representation is preserved.

The target retains deliveryDate and adds deliverAt, both with exactly the source purchased-goods delivery datetime description and identical official example. Target deliveryDate is deprecated in version 70 and explicitly says Use `deliverAt` instead. Either target carries the source concept under the published v72 schema; the migration-preferred spelling is deliverAt.
Both independently define an integer adjustment, positive or negative, added to the normal fraud score.
Both independently define the merchant account identifier used to process the transaction.
Both independently define a merchant reference linking multiple transactions and unique per billing cycle; the role differs from payment reference and first-partial-payment reference.
Both independently define the pspReference of the first partial gift-card payment used to link multiple payments.
Both independently define the recurring payment type and the Subscription, CardOnFile and UnscheduledCardOnFile roles.
Both independently define the merchant reference identifying one payment and used in payment-status communication.
Both independently define the shopper email address used in velocity/fraud checks.
Both independently define the shopper IP address used in risk checks and authentication requirements.
Both independently define the sales channel and whether the shopper is returning, with Ecommerce, ContAuth, Moto and POS meanings.
Both independently define payment language from a language code and country code.
Both independently define the merchant reference identifying the shopper, required for recurring payments and distinct from one-payment or one-order references.
Both independently define the text shown on the shopper bank statement.
Both independently define the ecommerce or point-of-sale store processing the payment.
Both independently define the shopper telephone number, with country-code requirements.
Both independently define performing only 3DS authentication without proceeding to payment authorization.

The source is a reference for aggregation of sales totals in reporting. Target merchantOrderReference links transactions for an order/billing cycle; target store identifies the processing store. The documented fallback to store is a default-value rule and does not make the dedicated sales-report aggregation reference identical to a store identity.
adyen_classic_payment52_to_checkout72.absence_scope: Selected top-level PaymentRequest scalar properties; full v72 PaymentRequest schema has no totalsGroup property. totalsGroup in BalanceCheckRequest is a different resource and is outside this case.

negative_contrasts.official_basis: Link multiple transactions; unique for each billing cycle.
The ecommerce or point-of-sale store processing the payment.

adyen_classic_payment52_to_checkout72.rationale: Both independently define routing the payment to a trusted MID.

The source chooses whether this transaction uses the Real-time Account Updater. The selected target booleans store payment details for recurring use or perform only authentication; neither selects account updating, and no named top-level v72 PaymentRequest scalar has that documented role.
adyen_classic_payment52_to_checkout72.absence_scope: Selected documented top-level PaymentRequest scalar properties; arbitrary additionalData keys are outside this projection and no undocumented key is assumed.

negative_contrasts.official_basis: Store payment details for future recurring payments.
Store payment details for recurring payments where the shopper is absent.
Perform 3D Secure authentication without payment authorization.
